html:
Abai Qunanbaiuly was a Kazakh poet, composer and thinker, the founder of modern written Kazakh literature. Kazakhs know him simply as Abai.

He was born in the steppe near Semipalatinsk, the son of a powerful local chief, at a time when the Kazakhs had come under the Russian Empire. He studied at a Muslim school and also learned Russian, and he came to admire both Islamic learning and Russian and European culture.

He translated poems by Pushkin, Lermontov and Krylov into Kazakh and set many of his own poems to music. His prose Book of Words is a set of short essays that criticise idleness, greed and feuding among his people, and urge them to learn and work.

The writer Mukhtar Auezov made his life the subject of the novel The Path of Abai. A region, a city and many streets in Kazakhstan carry his name.
sum: Abai Qunanbaiuly was a Kazakh poet, composer and thinker, the founder of modern written Kazakh literature. Kazakhs know him simply as Abai.
